transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thanks. I guess I’ve just been kind of more stressed than I expected lately. I’ve been trying to clean up my image and routine for some arts board stuff, and I’m still functioning, like I’m doing the basics, so it’s not… terrible or anything.

But I’ve been more tense and a little down, and I keep dropping small things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts. Then I feel guilty about it and end up canceling plans instead of just catching up. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing I should come in for, but it’s been bothering me.
Are you still enjoying the things you normally like to do?

I think… mostly, yeah, I still like them. It’s just harder to actually stay on top of them lately. Like with the fair planning notes or design drafts, those are things I normally care about, and I don’t hate doing them or anything. I just sort of let little pieces slip, and then I feel guilty and end up canceling plans instead of catching up.

So I guess I’m still interested, I’m just more tense and kind of down than I expected, if that makes sense.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?

Not most of the time, I don’t think… or, I’m not sure if I’d call it anxious exactly. I’ve just been more tense than usual since I started trying to clean up my image and routine for the arts board stuff.

I’m still doing the basics, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I keep dropping little things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts. Then I feel guilty and cancel plans instead of just catching up. Does that count as anxiety?
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but now you don't find pleasure in them anymore?

I don’t think so… not in the sense that I get no pleasure from them anymore. I still like the things I liked.

Maybe I’m a little less excited or I put things off more, but when I actually do them, I can still enjoy them. I hope that answers what you mean.
Have you lost any weight recently?
Um… I don’t think so. I haven’t really been tracking it closely, but my clothes don’t feel different or anything. I don’t think I’ve lost weight in any noticeable way.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

I wouldn’t say sad most of the day, exactly… maybe more down than usual. Since I started trying to clean up my image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and kind of low, and then I drop little things I care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts. Then I feel guilty and cancel plans instead of just catching up.

But I’m still doing the basics, so I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your current state?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I wouldn’t say I’m avoiding everything, but when I start feeling tense or down, I’ll cancel plans instead of catching up on the little things I’ve dropped.

Like with the arts board stuff, I’ve been trying to get my image and routine together, but then I fall behind on things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts. Then I feel guilty and it’s easier to just not go or not deal with it right away. I’m still doing the basic stuff, though. Does that make sense?
Do you often worry about things that are coming up in the future?

Yeah, I do… not constantly, I guess, but more than I used to. It’s mostly about things coming up with the arts board stuff and trying to keep my image and routine together.

I’ll think, like, “What if I fall behind again?” or “What if I mess up something small?” And then I get tense, and I end up dropping little things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts. Then I feel guilty and sometimes cancel plans instead of just catching up. I’m still doing the basics, though… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and won't go away?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the way you mean, I don’t think.

I’ll have worries come back up, like replaying whether I handled something okay, but it’s not like a thought that won’t leave me alone all day or anything. At least I haven’t noticed it that strongly. Is that what you’re asking about?
Are you avoiding certain situations because you fear something might happen?

I think… sort of, but not because I’m scared something terrible will happen. It’s more like I worry I’ll fall behind or look like I don’t have it together.

Since I’ve been trying to clean up my image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected. I’m still doing the basics, but I’ll drop smaller things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts. Then I feel guilty, and sometimes I cancel plans instead of catching up.

I know that probably sounds a little silly… but that’s more what it is.
Do you find yourself having thoughts or worries that keep coming back to you, even when you try to focus on other things?

I mean… not really in a big way, I don’t think. I can get distracted by worries and they’ll pop back up, but I wouldn’t say they’re stuck in my head no matter what I do.

Maybe I’m not explaining it right, but it feels more like normal worrying that’s been happening more lately, not like… uncontrollable thoughts. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel like you're on edge?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I’m still getting through the basic stuff.

But since I started trying to clean up my image and routine for the arts board things, I’ve been more tense than I expected. Kind of down too. I’ll be trying to keep up, and then I end up dropping smaller things I usually care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts, and then I feel guilty and sometimes cancel plans instead of just catching up.

So… on edge, yes, maybe. Not constantly, but more than I’d like.
Do you often have trouble sleeping due to worrying or feeling tense?

I’m not sure I’d say “often.” I mean, I have nights where I’m tense and it takes me a bit to settle down, but I don’t know if it’s enough to call it a real sleep problem.

I can usually sleep eventually. I don’t want to exaggerate it.
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your daily life?

A little, yeah. I’m still doing the basic errands and things I have to do, so I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart.

But I have noticed I’m not as reliable with the volunteer and creative stuff people usually count on me for… like fair planning, or following through on design things. I’ll mean to do it, and then I get caught up worrying or second-guessing, and it slips. So… I guess it is interfering some.
Do you feel like your worrying is significantly affecting your ability to function in your daily activities?

I think… not significantly in the sense that I’m still managing the basic errands and commitments. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function.

But it has affected some things. I’ve been less dependable with the volunteer and creative roles people usually count on me for, like the fair planning stuff and following through on design things. So… maybe not my whole daily life, but enough that I notice it, if that makes sense.
Do you find that you worry about things even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I worry for no reason exactly. Usually I can point to something, even if maybe I’m making it bigger in my head than it needs to be.

But if you mean worrying when nothing is actually happening right then, then… maybe sometimes. I just don’t want to overstate it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you experienced any significant life changes or stressors recently, aside from the arts board issues?

Not really… I mean, not that I can think of. Nothing big like a move or a breakup or anything. I guess just normal life stuff, but I don’t know if that counts.

I don’t want to miss something obvious, though—what kind of stressors do you mean?
Do you avoid social interactions or activities because you're afraid of what others might think of you?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I care what people think, probably more than I should sometimes, but I don’t usually avoid seeing people or doing things because of it.

If I skip something, it’s usually for some other reason, I think. But I’m not sure if I’m interpreting the question the way you mean it.
Do you think your tension and guilt are more related to the pressure of meeting expectations for the arts board, or are they more about worrying in general?

I think it’s more tied to the arts board expectations, yeah. Not just worrying in general.

Like… since I started trying to clean up my image and get my routine together for all of that, I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected. I’m still doing the basic stuff, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I keep letting little things slip—like planning notes for the fair, or design drafts I normally care about—and then I feel guilty and end up canceling plans instead of just catching up.

So I guess it’s mostly that pressure, if that makes sense.
Do you think your feelings of tension and being down would improve if the pressure from the arts board were to be removed or resolved?

I think it probably would help, yeah. I mean, the whole “reset” I’m trying to do is still actively happening, so it doesn’t feel like some totally separate thing that’s just continuing on its own after everything ended.

So… I guess if the arts board pressure got resolved, I’d hope I’d feel more like myself again. Does that answer what you mean?
